lead: >-
  Wildlife watching on a journey combining Bolivia, Chile, Colombia and Ecuador is concentrated in two countries: the Bolivian route visits high-altitude lagoons with flamingos, while Ecuador includes Galapagos marine excursions featuring birds, iguanas and sea lions. The Chilean segment focuses on the Atacama and the transfer toward Bolivia's border; the Colombian segment is mainly urban. A separate safari in each of the four countries is not part of the itinerary.

## Bolivia, Chile, Colombia and Ecuador: Where Wildlife Is Actually Observed

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining the four countries with the “Wildlife and Safari” interest. One of our routes is the [32-day tour through 8 South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Its overall theme includes natural areas and wildlife sightings, but **the individual country segments differ considerably**.

In [Bolivia](/bolivia/), the main nature experiences feature highland lagoons and flamingos. [Ecuador](/ecuador/) includes the Galapagos, where optional excursion routes offer opportunities to watch sea lions, birds and iguanas. In [Chile](/chile/), the Atacama landscapes and crossing into Bolivia are important; in [Colombia](/colombia/), this program focuses on cities and cultural stops. This differs significantly from tours designed specifically around one country's national parks.

The four selected countries are also **only part of the full eight-country tour**. The journey begins in Brazil and includes Argentina, Uruguay and Peru. Its duration cannot be calculated by simply adding up four nature excursions.

## Bolivia: Flamingos at Altitude and the Uyuni Salt Flat

After [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the itinerary crosses the border and uses 4×4 vehicles to explore Bolivia's high-altitude landscapes. Laguna Verde, **Laguna Colorada**, other saline and mineral lakes, geysers and desert areas are explicitly listed.

Flamingos can be observed around Laguna Colorada. This is one of the most specific birdwatching experiences on the Bolivian section, confirmed by the itinerary. Bolivia's official tourism portal also highlights the lakes and wildlife of the Eduardo Avaroa highland reserve. The **altitude, wind and cool weather** matter: this is a jeep excursion through the Andes, not a tropical safari.

The following day continues past lagoons and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Uyuni itself is best known for its unusual salt surface and vast views; the tour does not promise a separate extended search for rare animals there. [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) is devoted to city sightseeing and historical visits.

## Chile: Atacama Landscapes and a Logistical Connection

The Chilean part of this tour includes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a flight to Calama and a stop in [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The itinerary moves from the capital toward desert areas and allows time for acclimatization before Bolivia.

The Atacama's scenery belongs to the separate [“Nature” theme](/interests/nature/), while **wildlife watching in Chile is not listed as a dedicated excursion**. Flamingo sightings at Chilean lagoons should not be added simply because such experiences are possible in the region. On the confirmed itinerary, flamingos are primarily associated with the Bolivian highland section.

An astronomy excursion near San Pedro is offered separately for the evening and depends on confirmation, so it is not an automatically included part of the nature activities either.

## Ecuador: The Galapagos and Alternative Marine Excursions

After Peru, the itinerary continues to [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) and then via [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The islands offer far more opportunities to see wildlife in its natural habitat.

One day is reserved for a sea excursion, but there are **two alternatives**: [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach, **or** South Plaza and Cape Carrion. The specific option is confirmed after booking; the tour does not promise both at once. The first option focuses on frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies; the second features sea lions, iguanas and birds along the rocky shore.

The contrast is clear: in Bolivia, wildlife appears among high-altitude mineral lakes; in Ecuador, it lives in marine and island environments. In the archipelago, follow conservation rules, keep your distance from animals and do not plan extra landings without an approved route.

## Colombia: Cities Rather Than a Dedicated Safari

The Colombian section includes [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/), [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/), [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/). The program features views, urban walks and cultural attractions. **A national-park visit specifically to observe wild animals is not confirmed here.**

The “Wildlife and Safari” label thus belongs to the complete eight-country journey rather than to four separate wildlife-watching programs. Those interested specifically in Colombian fauna would need a different itinerary including identifiable natural areas.

## Where Wildlife Watching Is Possible on the Route

| Location | Wildlife-watching experience in the itinerary |
|---|---|
| Bolivia | Flamingos at high-altitude Laguna Colorada |
| Chile | No dedicated wildlife observation; the Atacama features scenery |
| Ecuador | Birds, iguanas and sea lions in the Galapagos; one of two alternative sea excursions |
| Colombia | No dedicated wildlife observation; urban and cultural program |

Consider the difference between the high-altitude Andean lagoons and the warm marine environment of the Galapagos when choosing dates. Bolivia requires warm clothing and wind protection, while the islands call for sea-trip clothing and sun protection. Any specific sighting depends on weather, season and the animals' behavior.

Compare [multi-country wildlife-watching tours](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) and the [“Wildlife and Safari” theme](/interests/wildlife/). Waterfalls, deserts and other landscapes feature in the separate [“Nature” collection](/interests/nature/). If the interest matters more than a particular country combination, start with confirmed wildlife activities and then choose the geography. The [unfiltered four-country selection](/multi-country/bolivia_chile_colombia_ecuador/) shows other available routes with the same combination, where applicable.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Wildlife in Four Countries

### Is flamingo watching included?

The Bolivian portion passes Laguna Colorada, where flamingos are one of the key natural attractions. Seeing a particular number of birds cannot be guaranteed.

### Do travelers visit both Seymour and South Plaza?

No. One of the two alternative Galapagos excursions is included; the choice is confirmed after booking.

### Is there a separate safari in Colombia?

On the confirmed eight-country itinerary, the Colombian section is mainly cultural and urban. Natural-park visits should not be assumed to be included.

### Can I travel through only these four countries?

The specified [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visits eight countries. A shorter journey limited to four would require its own itinerary and transport arrangements.

## Bolivia, Chile, Colombia and Peru: How the Journey Works

The key feature of this combination is **three consecutive Andean stages followed by a separate Colombian finale**. At [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the route approaches the highlands; around [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), it crosses salt flats and lagoons; and in Peru, it combines Titicaca, Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Much later, the journey continues through Colombia: Medellin, Cartagena and Bogota.

This selection displays current multi-country programs containing all four countries. It **does not mean the journey is limited to them**. For example, the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Ecuador. Quito and the Galapagos Islands lie between its Peruvian and Colombian sections.

When choosing, therefore, check the full route map and the number of nights in each region. A trip limited to only the four specified countries would need its own itinerary and duration.

## What Happens in Each Country

### Chile: Preparing for the Highland Stage

After Santiago, the journey passes through Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This stage is important because a 4×4 route through the Bolivian highlands begins next. Santiago and the Atacama require different clothing and involve different physical demands, so clothes suitable for the capital are not enough for an early departure toward the lagoons.

On the extensive tour, an evening astronomy excursion in the Atacama is optional and depends on observation conditions. It cannot be treated as a compulsory, prepaid activity. Travelers drawn primarily by the desert and night sky should also consider [tours in Chile](/chile/tour/) and compare them with the full route through Bolivia.

### Bolivia: Salt Flats, Lagoons and La Paz

The itinerary crosses [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), high-altitude lagoons, geysers and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The 4×4 section is followed by La Paz and the archaeological site of [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). This combines long road journeys with short walks at individual natural sites; it is not a multi-day walking trek unless separately specified.

Here altitude matters more than the distance between points on a map. Our itinerary includes time in San Pedro de Atacama before the Bolivian portion and warns about the possibility of altitude sickness. Planning helps reduce the abruptness of the transition, but cannot guarantee that symptoms will not occur. Travelers with cardiovascular or pulmonary conditions or other limitations should discuss the route and altitude with a physician before paying.

### Peru: From Titicaca to Machu Picchu

From Bolivia, travelers cross toward Puno and [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then take a tourist bus to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). The itinerary includes a train to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), visits to Inca monuments and a flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Transfers, train tickets and admission tickets are specified in the main tour terms; check the current description for their exact sequence.

Cusco and Bolivia's highlands call for similar care with acclimatization, but Peru's weather changes on the descent toward Lima. The rainy season around Cusco generally begins during Southern Hemisphere spring; for October–November travel, allow for weather changes and check current access requirements at archaeological sites.

### Colombia: City Experiences After Ecuador

In [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/), the itinerary includes a visit to [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/), followed by Comuna 13 and a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The final stops include [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), Monserrate and [Zipaquira](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) with its Salt Cathedral. Between Peru and Colombia, the route passes through Ecuador, including domestic flights and island excursions.

Cartagena is warmer and more humid than the high Andes. Packing needs to cover both lightweight clothing for the Caribbean coast and closed, warm clothes for Uyuni and early departures. One universal jacket will not be sufficient for all these conditions.

## What to Check Before Booking

**Sequence and duration.** On the complete 32-day tour, Chile, Bolivia and Peru follow one another, while Colombia comes after Ecuador. Cutting the trip to four countries would change flights, starting and finishing points and the number of nights. We can develop such an itinerary separately; four countries appearing together in the catalog does not imply an existing short version.

**Borders and documents.** Visa requirements, passport validity, onward-travel evidence and transit rules must be checked for the traveler's nationality and every actual border crossing. For holders of Russian international passports, these are four distinct entry countries, and the full program has eight. Requirements for one state cannot be assumed to apply in another, and a multi-flight ticket does not serve as a single border permit.

**Money.** Bolivia uses the boliviano, Chile the Chilean peso, Peru the sol and Colombia the Colombian peso. Even when much of the journey is prepaid in US dollars, travelers need payment methods for personal expenses. Verify acceptance of a particular foreign or Russian bank card before departure; plan cash reserves and currency exchange separately from the tour price.

**What's included.** The [main 32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) lists accommodation in 4-star hotels, domestic flights, transfers and the specified excursions. International flights, additional excursions, some meals and personal spending are listed separately. Guiding language changes by location: Uyuni and several other destinations have English-speaking guides. Russian-language guiding should not be promised throughout.

## Comparing the Program With Shorter Trips

If your main aim is **highland scenery and Inca heritage**, the Chile–Bolivia–Peru combination will be central to your choice, while Colombia adds substantial geographical reach. Travelers wanting to move from the Andes to colonial towns and the Caribbean coast will find a very different experience in the Colombian finale. In its full form, this is a major continental journey calling for comfort with frequent flights and sufficient time.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Open the main program and its current terms from the catalog:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

For other options, compare [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/), [Peru tours](/peru/tour/) and [multi-country itineraries](/multi-country/). These are different catalogs designed to help identify which parts of the journey you want to emphasize.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Bolivia, Chile, Colombia and Peru

### Is this an existing itinerary strictly limited to four countries?

The selection is built around countries on the main route. The [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also includes Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Ecuador. A route limited to four countries must be arranged separately.

### Can I go straight from Chile to Bolivia?

On the current extensive journey, travelers cross from the San Pedro de Atacama area toward Bolivia's highland lagoons. Dates, transport, altitude and border formalities need to be checked for the particular departure.

### Must I prepare for altitude even if I am not trekking?

Yes. Long drives at high altitude can also be demanding because of the thin air. The difference between the coast and the Altiplano deserves attention regardless of whether hiking is included.

### Does Colombia come immediately after Peru?

No. On the featured journey, Quito, the Galapagos Islands and Guayaquil form an Ecuadorian stage between Lima and Colombia. This includes separate flights and excursions and cannot simply be removed without changing the onward connections.

## Adventure in Bolivia, Chile, Colombia and Peru: What's Included?

The main active portion of the journey leads from [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) through [Bolivia's](/bolivia/) highland lagoons to the Uyuni Salt Flat. The route then continues via Titicaca to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and after other countries, to the mountain scenery around Medellin in Colombia.

We currently offer a [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The four countries in the catalog title form part of that itinerary, but **it is not a separate four-country program**. Before Chile, travelers visit Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay; Ecuador and the Galapagos lie between Peru and Colombia. Adventure activities complement a busy itinerary of nature, cultural and historical excursions.

## Chile and Bolivia: The Main Off-Road Journey

A city tour is planned in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), followed by a flight to Calama and a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama to acclimatize. An optional evening astronomy excursion can be arranged separately, subject to observation conditions and the lunar calendar.

After reaching the Bolivian border, the two-day 4×4 journey with an English-speaking guide begins. Day one visits [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Dali Desert, Polques thermal springs, the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The overnight stay is in an expedition-style hotel.

The next day combines the Honda, Chiarcota, Hedionda and Cañapa lagoons, the Ollague Volcano area, the Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Colchani and an island with giant cacti are also included. This is a **high-altitude vehicle expedition**, not a sporting trek on foot: some stretches lie above 4,000 meters, so the main physical factors are altitude, long journeys and changing weather.

After Uyuni comes a flight to La Paz, a city tour and the [Valley of the Moon](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/). The Bolivian stage ends with [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) en route to the Peruvian border.

## Peru: Mountain Roads, Titicaca and Machu Picchu

The crossing at Desaguadero takes travelers to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). An excursion to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) is planned. A tourist bus then crosses La Raya Pass, Raqchi, Sicuani and other stops on the way to Cusco.

A full day at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is scheduled from [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), with an English-speaking guide and a return train journey. A multi-day Inca Trail trek, mountaineering or trekking overnight stays are not included. Tolerance of mountain transfers and a packed sightseeing schedule matter more here than training for a sporting expedition.

## Colombia: Mountain Views and City Excursions

After Peru, the itinerary continues through Ecuador and only then reaches [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). From Medellin, an approximately eight-hour excursion visits a replica of old El Peñol, [El Peñon de Guatape](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/). Views of the reservoir accompany a stroll through the colorful town. The next stops are [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/).

The Colombian section is largely sightseeing: a visit to the rock does not mean independent rock climbing or a specialist mountaineering ascent. Bolivia's highlands remain the most physically demanding natural stage.

## Altitude, Borders and Packing

One journey involves many climate zones and elevations: the Atacama is dry, Bolivia's plateau has extreme temperature changes, and Colombia includes both mountain cities and the Caribbean coast. Warm layers, sun protection and comfortable shoes are required for the highlands. Anyone with a condition affecting altitude tolerance should consult a doctor before traveling; a stop in San Pedro for acclimatization does not guarantee protection from altitude sickness.

The key overland sequence is San Pedro de Atacama → Bolivia's lagoons → Uyuni → La Paz → Desaguadero → Puno. Border crossings, later flights, insurance and document validity must be coordinated for all eight countries. Visa rules depend on nationality, and acceptance of foreign or Russian bank cards varies by bank and country. There is no universal visa or payment method for every participant.

Ada Tours helps arrange the pace and order of the stages, allow buffers for connections and discuss extra activities separately. The actual flights, hotels, guides and included excursions are listed on the [tour page](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). If you want a dedicated sporting trek, compare [adventure itineraries](/interests/adventure/) by the activities involved, not just country names.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Adventure in Four Countries

### Do I have to drive the 4×4 myself in Bolivia?

No. The itinerary includes a two-day 4×4 trip with a guide; self-driving is not listed.

### Is the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu included?

No. A guided [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) excursion with a train journey back to Cusco is included.

### Are all four countries visited consecutively?

No. Chile, Bolivia and Peru follow one another, then the journey continues through Ecuador before reaching Colombia.

### What requires special preparation?

Elevations above 4,000 meters in Bolivia, the tightly scheduled journeys and different climates. Consider these in advance along with medical limitations and insurance conditions.

## Bolivia, Chile, Colombia and Peru: A Journey Through South America's Different Eras

This selection suits travelers wanting to combine colonial architecture, pre-Inca Andean cultures, Inca heritage and the history of modern Latin American cities in one journey. On the current program, [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) introduces Chile's capital, [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) offers a look at a civilization that preceded the Inca, [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) represent Inca heritage, while [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) reveal other chapters of the continent's history.

We currently offer a [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Bolivia, Chile, Colombia and Peru are **four main countries on a longer route**, which also includes Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Ecuador. Cultural excursions are spread throughout the trip, and Colombia follows Ecuador rather than immediately following Peru. This distinction matters when assessing time, flights and budget.

## Chile: From Santiago's Colonial Center to Its Modern Districts

A sightseeing tour of [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) includes the La Moneda Palace and Plaza de Armas area, providing an introduction to the city's early history. It continues over Santa Lucia Hill and through the modern Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia districts. In one day, travelers compare the historic center of the capital with its contemporary character.

On this itinerary, Chilean history is primarily represented by Santiago. The next section is a flight to Calama and a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama before entering Bolivia's highlands. A separate extensive archaeological program in the Atacama is not included. An optional excursion to Maipo Valley wineries is offered separately and should not be treated as part of the prepaid cultural day.

## Bolivia: Tiwanaku and Life in a Highland Capital

A [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) city tour includes the Witches' Market, followed by a visit to the [Valley of the Moon](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/). These stops introduce urban traditions and the unusual terrain around the capital, although the natural site itself is not a monument of an ancient civilization.

Bolivia's principal historic stop is [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), on the way to Peru's border. Its ceremonial structures, Kalasasaya temple and Gate of the Sun belong to a distinct pre-Hispanic Tiwanaku culture. It would be inaccurate to call its people simply “early Incas”: this was a different historical civilization, crucial to understanding the Andes before the Inca state.

On the same day, the group crosses the border at Desaguadero and continues to Puno. Thus the visit to Tiwanaku is combined with a demanding travel day rather than forming a multi-day archaeological expedition.

## Peru: Titicaca, Inca Culture and Colonial Lima

At [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the program includes the reed-built [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), introducing the traditions of the lake's inhabitants. On the way from Puno to Cusco, the tourist bus stops at Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, La Raya Pass and Pucara. The route moves between colonial religious architecture, Inca-era sites and earlier Andean traditions.

A separate day is dedicated to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) with an English-speaking guide. In [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the program visits [Qorikancha](/peru/place/coricancha/), Qenqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay and [Sacsayhuaman](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/). This is an organized sequence of specific monuments rather than simply free time in a historical city.

In [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), the program features Miraflores, Love Park, an exterior view of Huaca Huallamarca, the main square and Santo Domingo. Subject to availability, a visit to the Cathedral or MALI Museum is planned. This alternative cannot be represented as a compulsory visit to both.

## Colombia: From Medellin's History to Cartagena and Bogota

In [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/) and [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), the journey explores modern urban history. Next is [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), where the excursion covers the fortified old center, Castillo San Felipe de Barajas, and colonial-era streets and plazas. Cartagena's historic fortifications are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This stage tells a very different story from Inca stone sanctuaries and Tiwanaku: Caribbean trade and maritime defense.

In [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), the itinerary includes La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection and Monserrate. A separate day covers the Salt Cathedral at [Zipaquira](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). Museum opening days should be checked; the order of city visits can change. A museum appearing in the itinerary does not guarantee admission every day of the week.

## Choosing This Cultural Journey

The four countries bring together three historical threads particularly well: the pre-Inca civilization of Tiwanaku; the architecture and social life of Inca Peru; and the colonial and modern cities of Chile and Colombia. Together they provide a broader view of the continent than a trip only to Cusco or colonial Cartagena.

The trade-off is a large number of flights and road journeys. The Chile → Bolivia → Peru sequence contains a two-day high-altitude 4×4 route, while reaching Colombia involves traveling through Ecuador. Plan for altitude tolerance, time at monuments and possible schedule changes. Entry and transit requirements depend on nationality: documents must be checked for **all eight countries**, along with card acceptance, cash and insurance during the various stages.

Ada Tours helps coordinate transfers and excursion days. Exact service inclusions, guides and visit alternatives are listed in the [full itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). For other combinations and shorter durations, compare [culture and history journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/), focusing on actual sites and nights rather than just country lists.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Cultural Route

### Do Tiwanaku and Machu Picchu belong to the same civilization?

No. [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) belongs to a distinct pre-Inca culture, while [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is associated with the Inca civilization. Visiting them in sequence allows a comparison of different Andean eras.

### Can I restrict the itinerary to these four countries?

Our catalog groups trips passing through all four, but the current itinerary also visits four others. A shortened version requires separate logistical planning and a newly agreed set of services.

### Are Russian-speaking guides included?

The 32-day tour has Russian-speaking guides for some city excursions, including Santiago, La Paz, Cusco, Lima and Colombian cities. Other stages, including Machu Picchu, use English-speaking guides. Check the day-by-day description for details.

### Is one day enough for Machu Picchu?

The selected program has a dedicated day for Machu Picchu with a return to Cusco. A longer study of the site or special hiking routes would require a different pace and separate arrangements for available entry circuits.

## Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia: Nature Experiences on the Actual Route

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}, including [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The journey begins in Brazil, passes through Argentina and Uruguay, then visits Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador, and finishes in Colombia. The four selected countries **do not form a stand-alone 32-day itinerary**.

The main natural sequence is Chile's Atacama → Bolivia's lagoons and Uyuni → Peru's Andes and Titicaca. Colombia adds green hills and the reservoir near Guatape, but Ecuador lies between the Peruvian and Colombian stages.

Explore combinations in the [general four-country catalog](/multi-country/bolivia_chile_colombia_peru/) and further nature itineraries in the [“Nature” section](/interests/nature/).

## Chile: The Road to San Pedro de Atacama

Following a tour of [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the group flies to Calama and travels to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This is preparation for the high-altitude road. We offer an optional night-time astronomy excursion in the Atacama separately; it is not part of the compulsory itinerary.

The following morning begins the crossing into Bolivia and a two-day 4×4 journey. Simply visiting San Pedro de Atacama does not mean that all of Chile's famous desert attractions are included. Check the day-by-day program for the list of stops.

## Bolivia: Lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat

The 4×4 route passes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the [Salvador Dali Desert](/bolivia/place/salvador-dali-desert/), Polques springs, the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Accommodation is planned in an expedition-style hotel.

**High-altitude stretches exceed 4,000 meters.** Traveling by jeep does not remove the effects of altitude. For some travelers, this is the most serious consideration when choosing the entire tour.

On day two, the route includes additional lagoons, Ollague, the Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), including an island of giant cacti. A separate flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) follows. Colorful lakes, desert mountains and salt are Bolivia's principal natural features on this trip. Uyuni's mirror surface depends on weather and cannot be guaranteed.

## Peru: Titicaca and Historical Sites Among the Andes

From La Paz, the group travels via Tiwanaku and the border to [Puno and Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), visiting the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). A tourist bus then takes travelers to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) with stops in mountain areas.

Peru combines a high-altitude lake, Andean landscapes and a visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The Machu Picchu visit includes a train and guided excursion, but no separate multi-day trek is part of the confirmed itinerary. Acclimatization should be planned during the Bolivian section, before reaching Peru.

## Colombia: From Medellin to El Peñon Rock

After the Peruvian and Ecuadorian days, travelers arrive in [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). A visit to [El Peñon de Guatape](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/) is planned. The huge rock, green hills and inlets of the reservoir contrast with Bolivia's arid landscapes.

Climbing the rock's staircase, if possible, depends on access, available time and fitness. The journey then continues through [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), where urban experiences become the focus.

Warm clothes, sun protection and opportunities for rest at altitude are important in the desert highlands. In Colombia, lighter clothing may be appropriate. ## Frequently Asked Questions About Bolivia, Chile, Peru and Colombia

### Are Chile, Bolivia and Peru visited consecutively?

Yes. From San Pedro de Atacama, the route crosses Bolivia's lagoons to Uyuni, then continues via La Paz to Puno.

### How high are the Bolivian stages?

Some sections exceed 4,000 meters. Attention to wellbeing is necessary even when traveling by vehicle.

### Does Colombia immediately follow Peru?

No. An Ecuadorian stage lies between them on this 32-day program.

### Is there a separate trek to Machu Picchu?

No. The itinerary includes a train journey and a guided visit, without a multi-day walking route.
